newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon government reaches out to private sector.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon government reaches out to private sector.

text.p: Cameroon's government has reached out to the Central African nation's private business sector, with the first formal meeting between the two sides for over a decade.

Prime Minister Peter Musonge Mafany, 14 ministers and a special advisor of President Paul Biya met business leaders on Friday in the economic capital Douala and gave them a 30-page memorandum of government pledges.

These included easing administrative controls, cracking down on crime, restoration of business confidence, reform of commercial law, reform of the financial system and development of new financing instruments, fair company taxation and ensuring greater security within the law for investments.
The two sides, who met for six hours, agreed to set up a permanent secretariat to promote and maintain the dialogue.
Cameroon is in an election year. The government has just postponed parliamentary elections planned for March to allow time for opposition candidates to register.
President Paul Biya, who took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982, faces a presidential election later this year.
